Length check uses >= so a trimmed query of exactly 100 characters is rejected; the spec only rejects queries over 100.

The HTML search route builds SQL by interpolating the raw `q` into the query string (SQL injection). It bypasses Book.searchBooks, so the parameterised query, length limit and LIKE escaping are all skipped.
The validation error is returned with the default 200 status instead of 400.
The exactly-100-characters boundary test is skipped, which hides the off-by-one in searchBooks.

LIKE pattern is built from the untrimmed query, so trimming has no effect on matching; trimmed is computed on line 37 but unused.
/books/search is registered after /books/:id, so :id captures 'search', parseInt gives NaN, and the endpoint returns 404 and never runs the search.
Validation error is returned with the default 200 status; route tests expect 400.

HTML search builds SQL by interpolating the raw query, which is SQL injection and violates the spec's parameterised-query rule. It also bypasses Book.searchBooks, so trim, length limit, non-string rejection and LIKE escaping never apply.
HTML route coerces the query with String(), so ?q=a&q=b becomes 'a,b' and any length is accepted; array rejection and the 100-character limit are skipped.
SearchValidationError catch branch is unreachable because the handler never calls searchBooks, so invalid queries never get a 400.
